clippings.speaker: Jack Lemmon
clippings.quote: I always like to say that what Billy did so successfully was to grow a rose in a garbage pail, because he told a romance, he made you care about these two people, with their flaws—it’s interesting that both of them are flawed. And he made you care about them. At the same time, he made a hell of a lot of personal comment about our business society and our mores and behavior—and made the best picture of the year.
clippings.title: Jack Lemmon Looks Back on His Seven-Film Partnership with Billy Wilder
clippings.context: From Lally's 1993 phone interview with Lemmon for his Wilder biography Wilder Times (Holt, 1996); the full transcript was first posted on Lally's site in 2022.

clippings.speaker: Jack Lemmon
clippings.quote: I’d pop into the office any time I got an idea, and Billy would think about it and he’d smile a little and he’d say, “Wait and show me.” Whenever I had an idea, he’d always stop me from telling it and say, “Don’t tell me. I might misunderstand. No. Show me.” And he was always wide open.
clippings.title: Jack Lemmon Looks Back on His Seven-Film Partnership with Billy Wilder
clippings.context: Same 1993 Lally interview; Lemmon is answering whether he and Wilder discussed the character of C.C. Baxter before shooting.

clippings.speaker: Jack Lemmon
clippings.quote: I wished that Billy had been a little looser as the writer and let us overlap and charge it more, and screw the lines. But Billy the writer, I know, does not like to have any of his words not heard. … If I have to fault Billy at all, I would fault him on that minor level only.
clippings.title: Jack Lemmon Looks Back on His Seven-Film Partnership with Billy Wilder
clippings.context: Same 1993 Lally interview; Lemmon names The Front Page (1974) as one of his least favorite of their films and gives his one criticism of Wilder.

clippings.speaker: Jack Lemmon
clippings.quote: We (then) went to Billy’s office, and he looked and said, “Hello, girls.” I told him what we just did, and I said, “Not one girl batted an eyeball.” He said, “Don’t touch anything.”
clippings.title: In Retrospect: Hollywood Legend Jack Lemmon Looks Back on Making ‘Some Like It Hot’
clippings.context: 1993 interview by Judy Sloane (portions first published in Film Review Magazine); Lemmon and Tony Curtis had just tested their drag looks in the Goldwyn lot's ladies' room.

clippings.speaker: Jack Lemmon
clippings.quote: The best single piece of direction I’ve ever gotten came from Billy Wilder, while we were making ‘Some Like It Hot.’ It’s the scene just after I’ve become engaged to the Joe E. Brown character. … Billy handed me the maracas and said, ‘In your happiness and joy, you dance with these things.’ It was a stroke of genius. It served as both pause and punctuation.
clippings.title: Wilder With a Twist of Lemmon
clippings.context: Paul Freeman's 1994 report on a joint Q&A with Wilder and Lemmon at the Stanford Theatre, Palo Alto; Lemmon was handed a pair of maracas on stage.

clippings.speaker: Billy Wilder
clippings.quote: Nobody's perfect, but he came as close.
clippings.title: Remembering Jack Lemmon
clippings.context: Wilder's statement on Lemmon's death, issued through a spokesman and read on air by Larry King, who also relayed that Wilder was "saddened by the loss of his friend Jack Lemmon, a great actor an a wonderful man."

clippings.speaker: Billy Wilder
clippings.quote: He was a wonderful guy … I loved him dearly and he was the best actor I ever worked with.
clippings.title: Hollywood Remembers Jack Lemmon
clippings.context: Wilder speaking to the Los Angeles Times after Lemmon's death, as quoted in ABC News's roundup of tributes (June 29, 2001); ABC also reports Wilder told Variety's Army Archerd he couldn't pick a favorite of their films: "I choose them all."

clippings.speaker: Billy Wilder
clippings.quote: Jack Lemmon is a ham. And you can always trim a ham. Jack Lemmon always gives you everything.
clippings.title: JACK LEMMON 1925-2001 // Farewell to America's Everyman
clippings.context: Quoted in Lemmon's obituary as something Wilder "once said"; the original occasion is not given.

clippings.speaker: Billy Wilder
clippings.quote: He has his own opinion on things, but he's not bullheaded about it
clippings.title: Behind the Camera - The Apartment
clippings.context: Rob Nixon's TCM production history of The Apartment quotes Wilder on Lemmon's cooperativeness, without naming the original interview.

clippings.speaker: Billy Wilder
clippings.quote: Happiness is working with Jack Lemmon
clippings.title: Duncan Campbell on Jack Lemmon, a 'beautiful actor'
clippings.context: Wilder's much-repeated line, cited in the Guardian's report on Lemmon's death as how Wilder "once described him"; no original source located.

notes: Lopsided pair. Lemmon on Wilder is well documented in first-person interviews: Kevin Lally's full 1993 interview transcript (kevinlallyonfilm.com) is excellent and has more usable material, e.g. Wilder as "the biggest softie that ever walked", the Some Like It Hot preview where Wilder cut only one scene, Wilder talking him out of a scene in Save the Tiger, Wilder getting "more didactic" around Avanti!/Buddy Buddy, and "I don't know who was crazier, me or him." Wilder on Lemmon was much harder to find. Every Wilder quote here is secondhand: a spokesman's statement read on Larry King, an LA Times quote passed on by ABC News, and three undated lines repeated in obituaries and TCM. The best Wilder-on-Lemmon material is in Cameron Crowe's Conversations with Wilder (the chapter "Jack Lemmon was my Everyman"), Charlotte Chandler's Nobody's Perfect, and Ebert's 1974 interview "Billy Wilder on The Front Page". None of it was usable. The Crowe book isn't openly online except as blog excerpts (sheilaomalley.com reprints Wilder's Cukor/Lemmon "a little less" anecdote, not used because it's a blog copy of a book). rogerebert.com returned 403 for all interview pages (Billy Wilder on "The Front Page", Interview with Jack Lemmon, Movie buffs loved it). The Paris Review "Art of Screenwriting No. 1" interview with Wilder returned 403. The Vanity Fair 1999 Crowe excerpt is behind the VF archive login. The Variety (Army Archerd) and LA Times 2001 originals weren't reachable, so those quotes come via ABC News. The Television Academy 1998 Lemmon interview has a clip "on working with Billy Wilder" but it's video only, with no transcript. Crowe's Guardian essay "Billy and me: why I love The Apartment" (1999-12-03) only paraphrases Wilder about Lemmon (he wondered about giving Lemmon "a limp, or some physical deformity"), so it wasn't used. "Happiness is working with Jack Lemmon" is widely attributed but I never found its original source; it's included as secondhand via the Guardian. Also seen but not used: Tribune India (2001-07-15) quotes Lemmon in an unspecified 1969 interview: "I would like to spend the rest of my life doing nothing but Billy Wilder films." A CNN Live at Daybreak clip (2002-03-29) of Lemmon calling the maracas "the best single piece of comedy direction that I've ever received" duplicates the 1994 Freeman quote. PopCultureClassics.com reprints Paul Freeman's 1994 article; the original outlet isn't named. The St. Petersburg Times obituary reads like the New York Times obituary but carries no NYT credit on the page, so it's recorded as St. Petersburg Times.
